titleEn: Poly-B Pipe Replacement in Vancouver: Costs, Process, and Why 1985–1997 Homes Need It
titleZh: 温哥华Poly-B管道更换：费用、流程与1985–1997年住宅为何需要更换
excerptEn: Poly-B pipes fail without warning in thousands of Metro Vancouver homes built between 1985 and 1997. Insurance companies are increasingly requiring replacement before renewing coverage. Here is what Vancouver homeowners need to know.
excerptZh: 温哥华1985至1997年间建成的数千套住宅中，Poly-B管道随时可能发生故障。保险公司越来越普遍地要求在续保前更换管道。以下是温哥华业主需要了解的内容。

contentEn:
Poly-B (polybutylene) pipes were the plumbing standard for homes built across Metro Vancouver between 1985 and 1997. By the early 2000s, a class-action settlement in the United States had confirmed what many homeowners already knew: Poly-B fails — often without warning — through a process called oxidative degradation. The plastic becomes brittle, cracks, and can flood a home within hours. In British Columbia, insurers have been requiring Poly-B replacement as a condition of renewal since approximately 2020, and the requirement is now nearly universal among major carriers.

If your Vancouver home was built during that window and still has its original plumbing, you are likely in a race against time: the pipes are degrading every year, and the cost of a failure — water damage, mould, structural repair — far exceeds the cost of replacement.

What Is Poly-B Pipe and Why Does It Fail?

Polybutylene (Poly-B) is a plastic resin pipe commonly installed with acetal (plastic) fittings and crimp-style metal clamps. The problem is not the pipe itself in every case — it is the fittings and the chemical interaction between Poly-B and the chlorine in municipal water supplies. Over 10–25 years, chlorine causes the plastic to oxidize from the inside out. The fittings — which are often the first to fail — can develop micro-fractures that are invisible until a joint suddenly gives way.

The Town of Richmond, City of Vancouver, City of Surrey, and Metro Vancouver municipalities have all seen widespread Poly-B failures. There is no way to predict when a given pipe will fail — it can happen at any time, often during the night when water pressure is highest and no one is home to catch it early.

Signs Your Vancouver Home May Have Poly-B

  • Built between 1985 and 1997 — the peak Poly-B installation era in BC
  • Grey or white plastic pipes (1/2" to 1" diameter) visible in the basement, utility room, or at the main shutoff valve
  • Plastic fittings (acetal resin, often cream or black) at 90-degree bends and junctions
  • Metal crimp rings visible at pipe joints — these are a hallmark of Poly-B installation
  • Unexplained low water pressure — internal scaling from Poly-B deterioration
  • Brownish water — sediment from degrading pipe walls

If you are unsure whether your home has Poly-B, a licensed plumber can confirm with a visual inspection in under 30 minutes at low cost.

The Replacement Process: From Poly-B to PEX

Modern plumbing replacement uses PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) tubing, which is chlorine-resistant, flexible, and carries a manufacturer's warranty of 25+ years. A full re-pipe typically involves:

  1. Full home assessment — map the existing Poly-B layout and identify all affected runs
  2. Permit application — a plumbing permit from the relevant municipality (City of Vancouver, Richmond, Surrey, Burnaby, North Vancouver, etc.) is required for a full re-pipe
  3. Water shutoff coordination — the home's water must be shut off during the repipe (typically 1–3 days for a single-family home)
  4. Poly-B removal — all existing Poly-B pipe and fittings are cut out and disposed of
  5. PEX installation — new PEX tubing is run through walls, floors, and ceilings, connecting to the existing shutoff valve, water heater connections, and all fixtures
  6. Pressure test — the completed system is pressurized and held for 30 minutes to verify no leaks before closing walls
  7. City inspection — the municipality inspects the installation and issues a final occupancy or plumbing permit approval

Reno Stars manages the permit application and coordinates the city inspection as part of the standard project scope. The process is fully insured and backed by a project warranty.

Poly-B Replacement Costs in Vancouver (2026)

Costs vary by home size, number of fixtures, and whether walls need to be opened:

  • Condo / townhouse (1 bathroom): $4,000 – $7,000
  • Single-family home, 2 bathrooms: $7,000 – $11,000
  • Single-family home, 3+ bathrooms: $10,000 – $15,000+
  • With drywall repair and painting: add $2,000 – $6,000 depending on scope

Most Metro Vancouver homeowners pay between $8,000 and $13,000 for a complete single-family home re-pipe in 2026.

Insurance Requirements: What Vancouver Homeowners Need to Know

By 2026, the majority of BC home insurers will not renew a policy on a home with confirmed Poly-B plumbing without either:

  • A signed plumber's report confirming Poly-B has been replaced with PEX, or
  • A commitment to replace within a specified timeframe (typically 30–90 days)

Some insurers have gone further: Intact Insurance, Aviva Canada, and Belair Direct all include Poly-B replacement requirements in their eligibility criteria. Failure to disclose known Poly-B plumbing at policy renewal can also void coverage for any subsequent water damage claim.

Reno Stars has completed Poly-B replacement projects across Richmond, Surrey, Burnaby, North Vancouver, and Vancouver proper. We provide the plumber's report and municipal inspection sign-off that insurers require.

Does the City of Vancouver Require a Permit for Poly-B Replacement?

Yes. A plumbing permit is required for a full Poly-B to PEX re-pipe in the City of Vancouver and in all surrounding Metro Vancouver municipalities. The permit cost varies by municipality (typically $150–$500 depending on the scope). Reno Stars handles the permit application as part of every Poly-B replacement project — homeowners do not need to submit anything themselves.

After the work is completed, the municipality requires a final inspection. Reno Stars schedules this and provides the completed permit card and inspection report for the homeowner's insurance records.

Can You Just Replace the Fittings Instead of the Whole Pipe?

No — not as a reliable long-term solution. While some plumbers offer fitting replacement as a cheaper option ($1,500–$3,000), the pipe itself is also degrading. Fitting replacement addresses only the most obvious failure points. Within 2–5 years, other sections of the same degraded pipe will fail. A full PEX re-pipe is the only solution that satisfies insurance requirements and eliminates the risk of sudden pipe failure.

Frequently Asked Questions About Poly-B Replacement in Vancouver

How long does a full Poly-B to PEX re-pipe take?

A typical single-family home re-pipe takes 2–4 days of actual work. Permit processing adds 1–3 weeks depending on the municipality. Reno Stars projects typically reach completion — including final inspection — within 3–5 weeks of contract signing.

Will my home need to be torn apart to replace Poly-B pipes?

Not necessarily. Skilled plumbers route PEX through existing wall cavities, ceiling spaces, and under floors using minimal cut-in access points. Reno Stars patches and paints all access holes as part of the standard project scope. In most cases, only 4–8 small access panels need to be opened and repaired.

Does Poly-B replacement increase home value?

Yes. Homes with documented PEX plumbing and a clean municipal inspection record are more attractive to buyers and appraisers. Poly-B is now a known liability in the Vancouver real estate market — a home with confirmed PEX replacement and documentation commands a premium and closes faster than comparable homes with undisclosed Poly-B.

Is Poly-B pipe still used in new construction?

No. Polybutylene pipes were effectively discontinued for residential use in North America after the 2005 class-action settlement. All new Vancouver-area construction uses PEX, copper, or CPVC.

Will my home insurance cover Poly-B failure damage?

If you have an active policy and can demonstrate that the failure was sudden and unintentional, some insurers will cover the damage — minus the deductible. However, many policies now contain Poly-B exclusions or require replacement as a condition of coverage. After a Poly-B failure claim, insurers may non-renew the policy. Proactive replacement before any failure is the most financially sound path.

Have Poly-B pipes in your Vancouver-area home? Contact Reno Stars for a free, no-obligation Poly-B assessment and quote. We serve Vancouver, Richmond, North Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, and the broader Metro Vancouver area. All work is permitted, inspected, fully insured, and backed by Reno Stars' project warranty.
contentZh:
Poly-B（聚丁烯）管道是1985年至1997年间温哥华地区住宅建筑中使用的标准水管。到2000年代初期，美国的一起集体诉讼已证实了许多业主早已了解的事实：Poly-B会失效——而且往往毫无预兆——通过一个称为氧化降解的过程。塑料变得脆弱、龟裂，可能在数小时内导致房屋被淹。在不列颠哥伦比亚省，保险公司自大约2020年起就要求业主在续保前更换Poly-B管道，目前主要保险公司几乎都已实施这一要求。

如果您的温哥华住宅建于该时期且仍使用原始管道，您可能正在与时间赛跑：管道每年都在老化，发生故障的后果——水损、霉菌、结构修复——远超更换成本。

什么是Poly-B管道？为何会失效？

聚丁烯（Poly-B）是一种塑料树脂管，在1985年至1997年间在大温地区的住宅中广泛安装，通常配有乙缩醛（塑料）管件和压接式金属夹具。问题不在于管道本身——而是管件以及Poly-B与城市供水中氯之间的化学反应。经过10至25年，氯会导致塑料从内到外氧化。管件——往往是首先失效的部分——会产生微裂纹，在接头突然脱落之前完全不可见。

列治文、温哥华市、素里市以及大温地区各市镇都曾出现大范围的Poly-B失效事件。无法预测给定管道何时失效——它可能在任何时候发生，而且通常发生在深夜水压最高、无人察觉的时候。

温哥华住宅Poly-B管道的警示迹象

  • 建于1985至1997年间——BC省Poly-B安装的高峰期
  • 可见灰色或白色塑料管（直径1/2"至1"），出现在地下室、设备房或主截止阀处
  • 塑料管件（乙缩醛树脂，通常为奶油色或黑色），出现在90度弯头和接头处
  • 金属压接环——在管道接头处可见——这是Poly-B安装的标志
  • 不明原因的水压降低——Poly-B老化导致的内部结垢
  • 水色发褐——管道内壁老化脱落的沉积物

如果您不确定自家是否有Poly-B管道，持牌水管工可以在30分钟内通过目视检查确认，成本很低。

更换流程：从Poly-B到PEX

现代管道更换使用PEX（交联聚乙烯）管，其耐氯、柔韧，厂家保修期超过25年。全面管道重铺通常包括：

  1. 全面房屋评估——绘制现有Poly-B布局图并识别所有受影响管段
  2. 许可证申请——需要向相关市镇（温哥华市、列治文、素里、本拿比、北温哥华等）申请水管许可证
  3. 停水协调——重铺期间需关闭房屋供水（独立屋通常需1–3天）
  4. 拆除Poly-B——所有现有Poly-B管道和管件被切除并妥善处置
  5. PEX安装——新的PEX管道穿过墙壁、地板和天花板，连接到现有截止阀、热水器接口和所有装置
  6. 压力测试——完成的系统在封闭墙壁前加压并保持30分钟以确认无泄漏
  7. 市镇检查——市镇部门检查安装并出具最终占用许可证或水管许可证批准

Reno Stars将许可证申请和市镇检查协调作为标准项目范围的一部分。工程全程投保并提供项目保修。

温哥华Poly-B更换费用（2026年）

费用因房屋大小、装置数量和是否需要打开墙壁而异：

  • 公寓/联排别墅（1间卫生间）： $4,000 – $7,000
  • 独立屋，2间卫生间： $7,000 – $11,000
  • 独立屋，3间以上卫生间： $10,000 – $15,000+
  • 含 drywall 修复和油漆： 另加 $2,000 – $6,000（视范围而定）

2026年大温地区大多数独立屋的全面重铺费用在$8,000至$13,000之间。

保险要求：温哥华业主需要了解的事项

到2026年，大多数BC省房屋保险公司不会为已确认存在Poly-B水管的房屋续保，除非：

  • 持牌水管工签署报告确认Poly-B已更换为PEX，或
  • 在指定时间内（通常30至90天）承诺更换

部分保险公司更进一步：Intact Insurance、Aviva Canada和Belair Direct均在其承保资格标准中包含Poly-B更换要求。在续保时未披露已知Poly-B管道还可能导致后续水损索赔的保险失效。

Reno Stars已在列治文、素里、本拿比、北温哥华和温哥华本地完成多个Poly-B更换项目。我们提供保险公司所需的管道工报告和市镇检查签章。

温哥华市是否要求Poly-B更换必须有许可证？

是的。温哥华市及周边所有大温市镇要求全面Poly-B至PEX重铺必须申请水管许可证。许可证费用因市镇而异（通常为$150–$500，视范围而定）。Reno Stars在每个Poly-B更换项目中都包含许可证申请处理——业主无需自行提交任何材料。

工程完成后，市镇部门需要进行最终检查。Reno Stars安排检查并提供完成的许可证卡和检查报告，供业主留存作为保险记录。

只更换管件而不更换全部管道可以吗？

不可以——这不是可靠的长期解决方案。虽然一些水管工提供仅更换管件的更便宜方案（$1,500–$3,000），但管道本身也正在老化。管件更换只解决最明显的失效点。在2至5年内，同一老化管道的其他部分也将失效。全面PEX重铺是满足保险要求和消除管道突然失效风险的唯一方案。

温哥华Poly-B更换常见问题

全面Poly-B至PEX重铺需要多长时间？

典型独立屋的重铺需要2至4个工作日。许可证审批另需1至3周（视市镇而定）。Reno Stars项目通常在签订合同后的3至5周内完成——包括最终检查。

更换Poly-B管道需要拆墙吗？

不一定。熟练的水管工通过现有墙腔、天花板空间和地板布置PEX，只需打开少量切入检修口。Reno Stars将所有切入孔修复和油漆作为标准项目范围的一部分。在大多数情况下，只需打开和修复4至8个小型检修口。

Poly-B更换能增加房屋价值吗？

能。有文件证明已更换为PEX且持有干净市镇检查记录的房屋，对买家和评估师更具吸引力。Poly-B现在是温哥华房地产市场的已知责任——有Poly-B更换文件和记录的房屋比未披露Poly-B的可比房屋溢价更高、成交更快。

新建住宅还使用Poly-B管道吗？

不适用。聚丁烯管道在2005年集体诉讼后实际上已停止在北美住宅中使用。所有新的温哥华地区建筑均使用PEX、铜管或CPVC管。

房屋保险会覆盖Poly-B失效造成的损害吗？

如果您有有效保单且能证明失效是突然且非故意的，部分保险公司会赔偿损害（扣除免赔额）。但是，许多保单现在包含Poly-B除外责任或要求将更换作为承保条件。在Poly-B失效索赔后，保险公司可能不再续保。在任何失效发生之前主动更换是财务上最明智的选择。

您的温哥华地区住宅有Poly-B管道？联系Reno Stars获取免费、无压力的Poly-B评估和报价。我们服务温哥华、列治文、北温哥华、本拿比、素里及整个大温地区。所有工程均持牌、已检查、全程投保，并提供Reno Stars项目保修。
